text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.63% today as oil prices climbed on escalating Middle East tensions. Iran's attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and reported strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities spooked the market about potential supply disruptions, pushing global crude oil prices up to $125.44 per barrel—a significant jump from typical levels. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to higher revenues and profits, so the stock has tracked this broader energy rally higher.

This move is part of a much larger two-week run-up of 13.3%, driven by the compounding effect of geopolitical risk premiums layering onto an already-tight energy market. Forecasters are warning that diesel shortages could persist into 2027 due to the Iran conflict, which only reinforces expectations that oil and refined products will stay elevated, supporting sustained strength in producers' margins and stock prices.
